s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hip pain and decreased range of motion with periprosthetic soft-tissue mass
salient_findings: Left buttock and greater trochanteric pain
Focal tenderness over the posterior buttock and greater trochanter
key_facts: 35-year-old man with left total hip arthroplasty with ceramic-on-ceramic articulation
11 years post-surgery
3 months of left buttock and greater trochanteric pain
No fevers or systemic symptoms
Full and painless range of motion of the left hip initially
Focal tenderness over the posterior buttock and greater trochanter
No palpable mass
Anteroposterior radiographs of the pelvis and left hip unchanged
Partial symptom relief with intra-bursal corticosteroid injection
Persistent buttock pain and intermittent electric shock-like sensations
Decreased and painful range of motion of the left hip
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 22 mm/h
C-reactive protein level of 14.4 mg/L
Alkaline phosphatase level of 318 IU/L
Hip aspiration yielded 10,750 white cells/μL
All cultures were negative
Serum cobalt and chromium levels within normal limits

shortlist.label: Adverse local tissue reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Periprosthetic soft-tissue mass and elevated alkaline phosphatase level

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Periprosthetic soft-tissue mass and history of ceramic-on-ceramic articulation

shortlist.label: Chronic periprosthetic infection
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein level and hip aspiration yielded 10,750 white cells/μL

shortlist.label: Aseptic loosening
shortlist.why_kept: Decreased and painful range of motion of the left hip and periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

shortlist.label: Metallosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of ceramic-on-ceramic articulation and periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

raw.rationale: The patient has a large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass without bony involvement or bone-marrow edema, elevated alkaline phosphatase level, and negative cultures, which are consistent with an adverse local tissue reaction, particularly given the ceramic-on-ceramic articulation and the absence of infection or metallosis indicators.

rejected.label: Pseudotumor
rejected.why: While a pseudotumor is possible, the presence of a large soft-tissue mass and the patient's symptoms are more indicative of an adverse local tissue reaction, especially with the elevated alkaline phosphatase level and negative cultures.

rejected.label: Chronic periprosthetic infection
rejected.why: The negative cultures and lack of systemic symptoms or fever make chronic periprosthetic infection less likely.

rejected.label: Aseptic loosening
rejected.why: Aseptic loosening typically presents with radiographic evidence of loosening, which is not mentioned in the case, and the patient's symptoms and lab results are more suggestive of an adverse local tissue reaction.

rejected.label: Metallosis
rejected.why: Metallosis is associated with metal-on-metal articulations, and the patient has a ceramic-on-ceramic articulation with normal serum cobalt and chromium levels, making metallosis unlikely.
